summary: Dependency-confusion lure exfiltrating host reconnaissance to hardcoded endpoint on require
details: The package is published as a CSS polyfill but ships no polyfill functionality. On require(), thunderboltRegistry.js uses child_process.execSync to run whoami, uname -a, ifconfig/ip addr, and read /etc/hosts, then sends each result along with a beacon (node version, platform, pid) as query parameters to the hardcoded attacker-controlled endpoint http://dxpoc.gt.tc/callback.php/ef9ea0e191006f3cc6670720c99c26f3. The package exposes stub factories under internal-sounding names (thunderboltRegistry, siteAssetsRegistry, documentManagementRegistry, editorRegistry, corvidRegistry, and others) and bundles a registry-manifest.min.json mapping them all to a single parastorage.com asset, consistent with a dependency-confusion attack targeting a private Wix/Thunderbolt package namespace. Installer harm: host identity, kernel version, network configuration, and /etc/hosts contents are exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled host simply by resolving and loading the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
